git show.help: Read literal paths on the code host's current default branch, without a checkout. Files return UTF-8 content; directories (including '.') return immediate entry names and kinds. Missing paths return kind missing; binary or oversized objects omit content with status binary or too_large. Results include default_branch and commit; output is bounded by the member result limit. Uses the member credential on the host, both interactively and inside a command, without a lease or approval.

git prepare.help: Clone/checkout an isolated member workspace: a ticket branch `ticket/<key>` (--issue-url, with --repo for a ticket that belongs to no repository), a PR head (--pr-url, alone or together with --issue-url, which checks out the PR head), or an ad-hoc branch (--repo --branch). A repository is named by its path. Unfinished checkouts stay assigned to their work and requested branch; idle checkouts of the same repository are reused with their build caches. Call prepare every run and use the returned repo_path and branch: a path from an earlier run may now belong to another work. Unfinished Git state is kept, including an agent-created branch; an empty branch means detached HEAD. Member workspaces are worked on only inside a running GuildBotics command, whose isolated environment runs every git of them.

git commit.help: Commit already-staged changes with the member identity. Stage the files you want with plain git (e.g. ``git add``) first; this command commits only what is staged and applies the member name/email to that single commit without changing the repository's git config.

git publish.help: Commit already-staged changes with the member identity, then push. Stage the files you want with plain git (e.g. ``git add``) first; this commits only what is staged with the member name/email and pushes the branch using the member credential.

Changing interactive mode requires a human's request or approval for that ticket (--human-approved). Unsupported providers refuse either flag. Reads and updates return the ticket's own interactive setting and interactive_ancestor URL; clearing the setting does not override an interactive ancestor. Report that inherited state to the requester. 対話指定の切り替えは、そのチケットについて人が依頼・承認した場合だけ --human-approved を付けて行う。継承元がある間は対話のままなので、その結果を伝える。

ticket read.help: Read one bounded page of a ticket's resource: tickets (the ticket itself: key, tracker, repository, lane, ...), ticket_comments, ticket_attachments (the files its body and comments refer to: id, name, media_type, size, and referenced_by, `body` or a comment id), or ticket_pull_requests (the code host's pull requests that refer to it), or tracker_tickets (subject: tracker path; conditions: text with all whitespace-separated terms in title/body, state open|closed|all, label, page_size; items: URL, key, title, state, lane, labels, updated_at). Collections accept page_size (1-100). Results contain normalized items and continuation; reuse identical conditions for the next page. HTTP methods, headers, and GraphQL are not accepted.

Results contain normalized items and continuation; reuse identical conditions for the next page. HTTP methods, headers, and GraphQL are not accepted.

repo-info read.help: Read one bounded page of the repository's dependency_alerts, the repository named by its path. It accepts state (open by default, resolved, dismissed) and page_size (1-100, default 30). With an id condition, it returns that one alert and accepts no other condition or continuation. For formatted or JSON alerts, run repository/security_alerts in a ready command environment. Results contain normalized items and continuation; reuse identical conditions for the next page. HTTP methods, headers, and GraphQL are not accepted.
